summary: Add isolated external-assistant pairing and trusted-local revocable grant management without live issuance

replay.detail: Separate versioned assistant grant and revocation claims provide authoritative policy history; historical person grants retain their existing reader. Assistant requests and management must reach the authoritative grant issuer member.

schema.detail: Client-v0 adds disjoint person and assistant pairing requests and sessions, assistant grant policy models with a concrete PersonId issuer, challenge/device/capabilities metadata, and trusted-local grant inspect/revoke/policy operations.

rules.detail: Only the daemon-configured owning person through the trusted-local CLI manages assistant grants; absent owner configuration fails closed. Server-established harness and native-peer provenance prevents forged owner headers from enabling grant inspection or owner assistant-device enumeration; paired person devices cannot administer grants even over Unix. Deployment owner identity stays in external configuration, never a hardcoded public identity. Explicit closed read scopes, disclosure consent, bounded expiry and approval-once policy do not confer person authority or message permission.

compatibility.detail: Existing person wire shapes and profile semantics remain unchanged. The TypeScript SDK is a source break for general pairing callers: PairingBegin and PairedSession become untagged unions (PersonPairingBegin | AssistantPairingBegin and PersonPairedSession | AssistantPairedSession), so generic callers must narrow before reading person_id, and person_id becomes optional on shared projections; Rust person variants keep deny_unknown_fields. Generated SDK person callers use PersonPairingBegin/PersonPairedSession. Assistant grants require assistant.grants.v1 and never fall back to person pairing.

downtime.detail: Normal daemon replacement is sufficient; no live grant issuance or adapter deployment is part of this change.

manual.detail: Assistant completion uses a separate owner-only profile. Live issuance remains gated on reviewed read authorization, caller/disclosure policy, feasibility and coordinated kill acceptance; future send remains dormant.

recovery.detail: Assistant policy and revocation survive restart. A failed local credential commit requires trusted-local grant inspection/revocation before a fresh pairing; old local profiles remain intact.
